resources.title: Incident Postmortem Writer
resources.tagline: Turn a pipeline incident into a blameless postmortem with real action items.
resources.description: Structures incident notes into a blameless postmortem: timeline, impact, detection gap, contributing factors, and action items with owners and dates.
learning_objectives: Write a blameless timeline
Separate trigger from contributing factors
Convert findings into dated, owned action items
resources.body:
# Incident Postmortem Writer

## Structure
1. **Impact** — who/what, in business terms, with a duration.
2. **Timeline** — timestamped, factual, no blame.
3. **Detection** — how we found out; if a human told us, that's a gap.
4. **Contributing factors** — plural; incidents are rarely single-cause.
5. **Action items** — each with an owner and a date, and a "done" definition.

## Anti-pattern
"Be more careful" is not an action item. Change the system so a careful mistake
is harmless.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: SQL Review
resources.tagline: A review pass that catches correctness bugs before the query reaches production.
resources.description: Reviews a SQL statement for fan-out joins, NULL-unsafe predicates, implicit casts, non-deterministic ordering, and functions that silently change grain.

needs_improvement: The 11/12 evaluation with 0 false positives is self-reported on the author's own fixture; independent verification pending.

learning_objectives: Prove a join cannot fan out before writing it
Spot NULL-unsafe `NOT IN` and `=` predicates
State the grain of a result set in one sentence
resources.body:
# SQL Review

## The first question
*What is the grain of this result?* If the author can't answer, stop.

## Rules
1. Every join states its cardinality (1:1, N:1, N:N) and justifies it.
2. `NOT IN (subquery)` is banned where the subquery can return NULL — use `NOT EXISTS`.
3. Comparisons across types must be explicit casts, not implicit.
4. `ORDER BY` without `LIMIT` in a view is meaningless — drop it.
5. `SELECT *` in a persisted model freezes an unstable schema.

## Deliverable
Findings with the exact predicate, the failure case, and a rewritten clause.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: Airflow DAG Reviewer
resources.tagline: Review a DAG for idempotency, retry safety, and backfill behaviour.
resources.description: Checks a DAG for non-idempotent tasks, unsafe retries, missing catchup policy, ambiguous catchup/backfill semantics and unbounded concurrency.
learning_objectives: Make every task safe to re-run
Choose retries and timeouts deliberately
Predict what a backfill will do before running it
resources.body:
# Airflow DAG Reviewer

## The idempotency test
"If this task runs twice for the same logical date, is the output the same?"
If no, fix it before anything else — retries will happen.

## Checklist
1. Every task writes to a partition keyed by the logical date, or uses MERGE.
2. `catchup` is a deliberate choice, not a default.
3. Retries have a backoff; a task that retries instantly will hammer a downstream.
4. `max_active_runs` and pool limits prevent a backfill from starving the daily run.
5. Sensors use `reschedule`, not `poke`, so they don't hold a worker slot.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: Athena Partition Advisor
resources.tagline: Cut scanned bytes — the only thing Athena bills you for.
resources.description: Recommends partition projection, bucketing or file-layout changes to reduce Athena bytes-scanned, and writes the projection DDL.
learning_objectives: Read the scanned-bytes metric per query
Apply partition projection for high-cardinality columns
Compact small files to cut per-request overhead
resources.body:
# Athena Partition Advisor

## Bill model
You pay per TB scanned. Every recommendation is judged by "does this reduce
bytes scanned?" — nothing else matters.

## Levers, in order
1. Partition on the dominant filter column (usually date).
2. Partition projection instead of `MSCK REPAIR` for predictable layouts.
3. Compact small files — per-file overhead dominates at < 16 MB.
4. Columnar + compression (Parquet + snappy/zstd) — 10-100x vs CSV.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: AWS Glue Job Reviewer
resources.tagline: Review a Glue job for cost, DPU sizing, and bookmarks correctness.
resources.description: Reviews Glue/Spark jobs for worker sizing, job bookmarks, partition pruning, and the catalogue/schema pitfalls that cause silent full reprocessing.
learning_objectives: Size Glue workers from data volume, not habit
Use job bookmarks correctly
Avoid full-table reprocessing from catalogue mistakes
resources.body:
# AWS Glue Job Reviewer

## Sizing
Start at 2x the number of input files' partitions, then watch the task histogram.
Over-provisioned workers are the most common Glue cost leak.

## Bookmarks
A bookmark only helps if the input path layout is stable. A renamed prefix
silently resets the bookmark → full reprocess.

## Catalogue trap
If the Glue Data Catalog schema drifts from the actual Parquet schema, readers
drop columns silently. Diff the catalogue schema against the file footer.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: Cost Unit-Economics Reporter
resources.tagline: Attribute pipeline cost per row, per table, per team.
resources.description: Turns cluster/warehouse billing into unit economics (cost per 1M rows, per run, per model) so a 4x regression shows up as a number, not a surprise invoice.
learning_objectives: Attribute compute cost to a pipeline run
Define a unit metric that resists regressions
Set an alert on cost-per-run, not on total spend
resources.body:
# Cost Unit-Economics Reporter

## Unit metrics that don't lie
- $ per pipeline run (stable denominator)
- $ per 1M rows processed
- DBU/credits per model build

## Why total spend is the wrong alert
Total spend rises with growth and hides regressions. Cost-per-unit is flat when
growth is healthy and spikes the day a join starts fanning out.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: Data Contract Author
resources.tagline: Turn a vague producer/consumer agreement into an enforceable contract.
resources.description: Drafts a data contract (schema, semantics, freshness SLA, ownership, breaking- change policy) and the tests that enforce it in CI.
learning_objectives: Specify a freshness and completeness SLA
Encode a contract as executable tests
Define a breaking-change policy consumers can rely on
resources.body:
# Data Contract Author

## A contract has six parts
1. Owner (a team, with an on-call).
2. Schema (typed, versioned).
3. Semantics (what each field *means*, units, nullability).
4. SLA (freshness, completeness).
5. Breaking-change policy (notice period, deprecation path).
6. Enforcement (which CI test fails on violation).

## Rule
A contract with no enforcement is documentation. Documentation is not a contract.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: dbt Model Review
resources.tagline: Review a dbt model for grain, materialisation, and incremental correctness.
resources.description: Checks a dbt model's grain statement, ref/dependency hygiene, incremental strategy and late-arriving-data handling, then proposes a test set.
learning_objectives: State a model's grain and match it to its unique key test
Choose table vs incremental vs view deliberately
Handle late data in an incremental model
resources.body:
# dbt Model Review

## Grain first
Every model must answer: "one row = one ___". The `unique` test goes on that key.

## Materialisation picker
- `view` — cheap, and the model is small or rarely queried.
- `table` — the source is huge and consumers need speed.
- `incremental` — the source grows monotonically and you can define the watermark.

## Incremental traps
1. Late-arriving rows older than the watermark are silently dropped. Add a
   lookback window (e.g. `>= max(updated_at) - interval '3 days'`).
2. `is_incremental()` must guard the filter or every full run is a full reload.
3. Deletes never arrive. Decide explicitly: soft-delete, or periodic full-refresh.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: Delta Optimization Advisor
resources.tagline: OPTIMIZE, Z-ORDER, or nothing — decide with data, not vibes.
resources.description: Reads Delta table history and file statistics to decide between OPTIMIZE, Z-ORDER, liquid clustering and partitioning changes.
learning_objectives: Decide if a table needs OPTIMIZE from file stats
Choose Z-ORDER columns from query predicates
Know when liquid clustering beats partitioning
resources.body:
# Delta Optimization Advisor

## Decide
- Files < 32 MB and many → `OPTIMIZE`.
- Queries filter on 1-2 high-cardinality columns → `ZORDER BY` those columns.
- High-cardinality, many predicates, frequent writes → liquid clustering.
- Predicate on one low-cardinality column (date) → partition (or leave it; Delta
  handles pruning well already).

## Measure
Compare `numFiles` and query `bytes scanned` before and after. If scanning
didn't drop, the Z-ORDER was on the wrong columns.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: Lineage Explainer
resources.tagline: Answer "what breaks if I change this column?" with evidence.
resources.description: Traces column-level lineage from an asset to its upstream sources and downstream consumers, and reports the impact set for a proposed change.
learning_objectives: Read the lineages of an asset from a lineage store
Compute a downstream impact set
Distinguish technical from business lineage
resources.body:
# Lineage Explainer

## Two questions, two graphs
- **Technical lineage** — which tables/jobs depend on this column.
- **Business lineage** — which metrics/reports depend on it.

A breaking change needs both, because a CFO does not read table names.

## Impact set
Walk downstream from the changed node, stopping at published marts. Report
owner, criticality, and the earliest SLA that will break.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: PII Classifier
resources.tagline: Find PII in a dataset and propose the masking policy.
resources.description: Scans column names and sample values for PII categories, then proposes classification tags and a masking/pseudonymisation policy.
learning_objectives: Classify columns into PII categories
Choose masking vs hashing vs tokenisation
Record a data-classification tag
resources.body:
# PII Classifier

## Caution
Sampling real data to find PII is itself a privacy action. Prefer metadata-only
heuristics first; only sample with authorisation, and never persist samples.

## Categories
Direct identifiers (name, email, phone, national ID), quasi-identifiers
(postcode, DOB), sensitive attributes (health, financial), and free text
(which can contain anything).

## Policy mapping
Direct → mask or tokenise. Quasi → generalise. Free text → never expose raw in
analytics; store separately with restricted access.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: Pipeline Test Author
resources.tagline: Write integration tests for a pipeline that run in seconds, offline.
resources.description: Builds a local DuckDB/pyarrow harness with tiny fixtures so pipeline logic is testable in CI without a cluster, and asserts on invariants, not snapshots.
learning_objectives: Test a transform without a Spark cluster
Assert invariants instead of golden files
Make a pipeline test deterministic
resources.body:
# Pipeline Test Author

## The harness
Keep fixtures as 3-10 row Parquet/CSV files under `tests/data/`. Load them with
DuckDB or pyarrow. No cluster, no network, < 2s.

## Assert invariants, not snapshots
- `count(*)` is stable across a re-run (idempotency)
- no nulls in the grain key
- sum(revenue) equals the source sum within tolerance
- a quarantined row never appears in the published table

## Rule
If a test needs the network or a running warehouse, it is not a unit test.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: Schema Change Contract Review
resources.tagline: Classify a schema change as safe, risky, or breaking — before it ships.
resources.description: Diffs an old and new schema, classifies the change (compatible / risky / breaking) against consumers, and produces the migration and comms plan.
learning_objectives: Apply backward/forward compatibility rules to a diff
Detect a breaking change hidden behind a "safe" rename
Write a deprecation plan with dates
resources.body:
# Schema Change Contract Review

## Classification
- **Compatible** — new nullable column, widened type that preserves values.
- **Risky** — narrowing a type, adding a NOT NULL without a default, changing units.
- **Breaking** — rename, remove, or semantic change to an existing column.

## The hidden breaking change
A rename + a new column with the old name looks compatible to a schema differ
but breaks every consumer that read the old semantics. Always diff *semantics*,
not just names.

## Migration skeleton
Add → dual-write → backfill → announce → migrate consumers → remove (dated).
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: Spark Data Quality Review
resources.tagline: Audit a PySpark job for silent data-quality failures before it ships.
resources.description: A review skill an agent runs against a Spark/PySpark transform. It checks null propagation, join fan-out, silent type coercion, non-deterministic row counts and missing post-write assertions, then reports findings as a diff-level list.
learning_objectives: Identify the five classes of silent failure in a Spark transform
Add pre/post row-count and null assertions to a job
Recognise join fan-out caused by non-unique keys
resources.body:
# Spark Data Quality Review

## When to use
Run this when a PySpark transform is about to be merged, or when a downstream
table's row count changed without a code change.

## Check order
1. **Null propagation** — every outer join introduces nullable right-side keys.
   Confirm downstream code coalesces or filters them.
2. **Join fan-out** — assert key uniqueness on the intended 1-side before joining.
3. **Silent coercion** — `cast` failures return null, not errors. Prefer `try_cast`
   and count the nulls it produces.
4. **Non-determinism** — `dropDuplicates` without a sort key keeps an arbitrary row.
5. **Missing assertions** — every write should be followed by a row-count and a
   null-rate check on the primary key.

## Output
A findings list: `severity | file:line | rule | suggested patch`.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: SQL Query Plan Explainer
resources.tagline: Translate an EXPLAIN plan into plain language and the one change worth making.
resources.description: Reads EXPLAIN / EXPLAIN ANALYZE output and explains scans, joins, spills and estimated-vs-actual row skew, then proposes the single highest-impact change.
learning_objectives: Read a plan bottom-up and name the expensive node
Detect cardinality misestimation from stale statistics
Decide between an index, a rewrite, or a stats refresh
resources.body:
# SQL Query Plan Explainer

## Method
1. Read bottom-up; the deepest node is the first data touched.
2. Compare `rows` (estimate) to `actual rows`. >10x off means stale stats.
3. Look for `Seq Scan` on a large table that should use an index.
4. Look for `Sort` / `Hash` spilling to disk (`disk usage` in the plan).

## Output
One sentence per expensive node, then exactly one recommended change with
the expected effect and a way to measure it.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: Backfill Planner
resources.tagline: Plan a backfill that doesn't melt production or corrupt the target.
resources.description: Produces a backfill plan: date ranges, blast radius, resource contention, idempotency check, validation gates and rollback.
learning_objectives: Scope a backfill by date and by dependency
Detect which downstream tables must also be rebuilt
Stage a backfill gradually with validation between batches
resources.body:
# Backfill Planner

## Before running anything
1. **Why** — which dates are wrong, and what does "correct" look like?
2. **Blast radius** — list every downstream model/table that reads the target.
3. **Contention** — will this run beside the daily job? At what hour is the cluster idle?
4. **Idempotency** — can each date be re-run safely?
5. **Rollback** — snapshot the target, or write to a shadow table first.

## Execution
Backfill in date batches, smallest first, validating a sample after each batch.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: CDC Merge Designer
resources.tagline: Design a correct upsert/delete merge from a change stream.
resources.description: Produces a MERGE (or Delta/Iceberg merge) that applies inserts, updates and deletes from a CDC stream correctly, including out-of-order events and tombstones.
learning_objectives: Order change events deterministically
Handle deletes (tombstones) without losing history
Make the merge idempotent under replay
resources.body:
# CDC Merge Designer

## Ordering
Events arrive out of order. Rank by `(lsn, ts_ms)` — never by ingestion time.

## Deduplicate before merging
Keep the latest event per primary key with a window function, then merge once.

## Deletes
A delete is an event with `op = 'd'`. Two valid choices:
- hard delete on merge, or
- soft delete + `_deleted_at` (required if you need history or audit).

## Idempotency
Re-running the same micro-batch must produce the same table. Ranking by LSN
guarantees this; ranking by arrival time does not.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: Iceberg Table Maintenance
resources.tagline: Keep an Iceberg table fast — compaction, snapshots, and manifest hygiene.
resources.description: Diagnoses small-file and manifest bloat and generates the compaction, snapshot expiry and orphan-file cleanup plan for an Iceberg table.
learning_objectives: Read an Iceberg metadata table to size the problem
Pick a compaction strategy and rewrite interval
Expire snapshots without breaking time travel
resources.body:
# Iceberg Table Maintenance

## Diagnose from metadata
```sql
SELECT count(*) files, avg(file_size_in_bytes)/1e6 avg_mb
FROM db.tbl.files;
```
avg_mb < 32 and a growing count → compact.

## Plan
1. `rewrite_data_files` with a target size (128-256 MB).
2. `rewrite_manifests` when the manifest list is huge.
3. `expire_snapshots` older than the retention window — but keep at least one
   full snapshot for time travel.
4. `remove_orphan_files` on a schedule, with a safety margin.

## Do not
Run compaction during peak ingestion; it conflicts with concurrent writers.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: Kafka Consumer Lag Triage
resources.tagline: Decide whether lag is a capacity problem, a poison message, or skew.
resources.description: Triages consumer lag from the consumer-group offsets: distinguishing a slow consumer, a partitioned hot key, a rebalance storm, and a poison-pill retry loop.
learning_objectives: Read per-partition lag to separate skew from throughput
Detect a rebalance loop from consumer-group state
Find the poison message from retry counts
resources.body:
# Kafka Consumer Lag Triage

## Three questions
1. Is lag rising, flat, or falling? Flat at a high number is fine; rising is not.
2. Is lag even across partitions? Skew means a hot key, not capacity.
3. Is the consumer group stable? Frequent `PreparingRebalance` is the real bug.

## Signatures
- Lag on one partition only → key skew; re-key or increase partitions.
- All partitions rising, CPU low → downstream (DB/API) is the bottleneck.
- Lag resets to zero then climbs → rebalance loop; check `session.timeout.ms`.
- One offset stuck, others advance → poison message in a retry loop.

## Never
Do not "fix" lag by resetting offsets. That is data loss wearing a hat.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: MCP Tool Contract Auditor
resources.tagline: Review an MCP server's tools for blast radius before you connect it.
resources.description: Inspects an MCP server's tool list and schemas, flags tools that can write, delete, spend money or exfiltrate data, and produces a least-privilege connection recommendation.
learning_objectives: Read a tool schema and predict its side effects
Classify tools by blast radius
Write a least-privilege MCP configuration
resources.body:
# MCP Tool Contract Auditor

## Classify every tool
- **Read** — safe, still logs the data it can reach.
- **Write** — can mutate state; needs a sandbox or a dry-run.
- **Destructive** — delete/drop/truncate; require human confirmation.
- **Spend** — provisions resources or runs billable queries.
- **Exfiltrate** — can send data to an external network.

## Deliverable
A table of tools by class, then a config that grants only the Read/Write tools
the task needs. Never connect an unvetted server with broad credentials.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: Spark Cost Regression Guard
resources.tagline: Detect the 4x cost jump in CI, before it reaches the invoice.
resources.description: Compares a job's shuffle/spill/scan metrics against a stored baseline and fails the change if cost-per-run regresses beyond a threshold, with the diff explained.
learning_objectives: Capture cost-relevant metrics from a Spark run
Store and compare a baseline
Explain which stage caused a regression
resources.body:
# Spark Cost Regression Guard

## Metrics worth baselining
shuffle read/write bytes, spill (disk) bytes, task count, max task duration,
input bytes. These predict cost far better than wall-clock time.

## Threshold
Fail if any metric grows > 25% vs the stored median of the last 5 runs. A 4x
regression is then caught at 1.25x, in CI, for free.

## Explain the diff
Name the stage whose metric moved, and whether it was a join, an aggregation,
or a partition count change.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: Spark Skew Diagnosis
resources.tagline: Turn "one task is 40 minutes behind" into a named root cause and a fix.
resources.description: Walks an agent through reading the Spark UI/event log to distinguish key skew, partition skew, and shuffle-write amplification, then selects between salting, AQE skew join, broadcast, and repartition strategies.
learning_objectives: Read task-level duration histograms to confirm skew
Choose between AQE skew join, salting and broadcast
Reproduce skew locally with a bounded dataset
resources.body:
# Spark Skew Diagnosis

## Signals
- Median task duration ~p50, but p99 is 30x+ → key skew.
- All tasks slow and shuffle read is huge → partition/scan problem, not skew.
- One executor at 100% while others idle → hot partition.

## Decision order
1. Confirm with `spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled=true` — if it fixes it, ship that.
2. If not, salt the hot key on both sides and aggregate twice.
3. Broadcast only if the small side is < 100 MB *after* filtering.
4. Never `repartition(1)` to "fix" skew; it serialises the stage.

## Evidence to attach
The task-duration histogram, the shuffle read/write bytes, and the top-10 keys
by row count — the review is not complete without them.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: Warehouse Clustering Advisor
resources.tagline: Choose warehouse size, clustering keys, and caching — measured.
resources.description: Advises on Snowflake/BigQuery/Redshift tuning: clustering keys, warehouse sizing, result caching, and the difference between a scan problem and a compute problem.
learning_objectives: Separate scan inefficiency from compute inefficiency
Choose a clustering key from predicate selectivity
Right-size a virtual warehouse from queue time
resources.body:
# Warehouse Clustering Advisor

## Diagnose first
- Query scans far more partitions than it needs → clustering/partition problem.
- Scan is optimal but the query waits → warehouse sizing or concurrency problem.

## Clustering key choice
Pick the column that appears in the WHERE clause of the *most expensive* queries,
with reasonable cardinality. Order matters: put the most selective first.

## Right-sizing from queue time
If queue time >> execution time for short queries, scale out (more clusters),
not up (bigger warehouse). Different problems, different knobs.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: DuckDB / MotherDuck MCP Server
resources.description: Queries DuckDB databases and MotherDuck, including reading Parquet/CSV directly from object storage. Excellent for local, offline analysis with an agent.

environment_variables.name: MOTHERDUCK_TOKEN
environment_variables.description: Only required if connecting to MotherDuck.

resources.security_notes: Reads/writes files it is pointed at. With `--read-only` it is safe for untrusted prompts. Without it, an agent can modify or drop local tables.

resources.title: Fetch MCP Server
resources.description: Retrieves a URL and converts it to markdown for the model. Commonly used to read documentation during a task.
resources.security_notes: Network egress to arbitrary URLs. In a corporate environment, route it through an allowlisting proxy; otherwise it can reach internal endpoints (SSRF risk).

resources.title: Filesystem MCP Server
resources.description: Reference server that exposes a sandboxed set of directories as readable and (optionally) writable tools. Useful for pipelines that operate on local files.
resources.security_notes: Grants read/write within the directories you pass as arguments. Scope it to a single working directory; never pass a home directory or a mount containing secrets.

resources.title: Git MCP Server
resources.description: Exposes local Git operations — status, diff, log, commit, branch — as tools, so an agent can inspect history and prepare changes without shelling out blindly.
resources.security_notes: Can commit and create branches in the scoped repository. It cannot push unless credentials are also present in the environment.

resources.title: GitHub MCP Server
resources.description: First-party GitHub server exposing repositories, issues, pull requests and code search, plus optional write operations.

environment_variables.name: GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
environment_variables.description: PAT or fine-grained token; scope defines blast radius.

resources.security_notes: Requires a GitHub token. Use a fine-grained token limited to the target repositories and read-only unless the task must open PRs. Never grant org-wide admin.

resources.title: PostgreSQL MCP Server
resources.description: Connects an agent to a Postgres database with a read-only query tool and schema introspection. The canonical example of a "database over MCP" server.

environment_variables.name: DATABASE_URL
environment_variables.description: Connection string. Use a read-only role.

resources.security_notes: The reference server issues raw SQL. Connect with a role that only has SELECT on the schemas intended, and prefer a replica. Do not point it at production with a superuser.

resources.title: BigQuery MCP Server
resources.description: Community server for BigQuery that lists datasets and runs SQL against a project, with support for the BigQuery SQL dialect.

environment_variables.name: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
environment_variables.description: Path to a service-account key with BigQuery roles.

resources.security_notes: Queries are billable. Grant `bigquery.dataViewer` + `bigquery.jobUser` only, set a custom quota, and consider `maximum_bytes_billed` on every job.
resources.note: Community project — review the source before granting credentials.

resources.title: DataHub MCP Server
resources.description: Exposes a DataHub catalog: search entities, read lineage and schema, and inspect metadata, so an agent can answer "what is this table and what depends on it?".

environment_variables.name: DATAHUB_GMS_URL
environment_variables.description: URL of the DataHub GMS endpoint.

resources.security_notes: Read-only against the catalog, but catalogue metadata can itself be sensitive (PII tags, internal table names). Use a scoped token and keep the GMS endpoint internal.

resources.title: dbt MCP Server
resources.description: dbt Labs server that exposes project discovery, the semantic layer, and the dbt CLI (`run`, `test`, `compile`) as tools, so an agent can build and inspect models.

environment_variables.name: DBT_PROFILES_DIR
environment_variables.description: Path to the dbt profiles directory.

resources.security_notes: Running `dbt run` executes arbitrary SQL against your warehouse with the credentials in profiles.yml. Point it at a dev target, never prod, and treat `--full-refresh` as a destructive operation.

resources.title: Snowflake MCP Server (Labs)
resources.description: Snowflake Labs server exposing object management and SQL execution against a Snowflake account, including Cortex Search and Analyst services.

environment_variables.name: SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH
environment_variables.description: Key-pair auth key; prefer key-pair over password.

resources.security_notes: Exposes create/drop tooling and billable query execution. Use a dedicated service user with a least-privilege role, a resource monitor with a hard credit cap, and a read-only role by default.

resources.title: AWS MCP Servers (Labs)
resources.description: A suite of AWS Labs servers — including documentation search, CDK/Terraform assistance, and service-specific servers — for agents working on AWS.

environment_variables.name: AWS_PROFILE
environment_variables.description: Named profile whose IAM permissions define what is reachable.

resources.security_notes: Server capabilities vary widely; some can create resources. Bind to a dedicated AWS profile with least privilege, use short-lived SSO credentials, and never attach an admin role. Treat resource-creating tools as requiring human confirmation.

resources.title: Kafka MCP Server
resources.description: Community server for Apache Kafka that lists topics, reads consumer-group lag, and samples messages, for stream debugging from an agent.

environment_variables.name: KAFKA_SASL_USER
environment_variables.description: SASL user, if the cluster requires it.

resources.security_notes: Sampling messages can expose production PII in the agent's context. Grant a read-only principal, prefer a topic allow-list, and never sample topics containing personal data without masking.
resources.note: Retargeted 2026-10-10 from dead kafka-mcp/kafka-mcp-server to tuannvm/kafka-mcp-server (Go, release v2.0.2, MIT badge in README; no LICENSE file in repo and API license detection disagrees — verify before commercial use). Not affiliated with the ASF. Review before use.

resources.title: Destructive SQL Guard
resources.description: Intercept DROP / TRUNCATE / DELETE-without-WHERE before an agent executes it.
resources.summary: Intercept DROP / TRUNCATE / DELETE-without-WHERE before an agent executes it.
resources.purpose: Intercept DROP / TRUNCATE / DELETE-without-WHERE before an agent executes it.
resources.implementation:
Matches the SQL string passed to a database/MCP tool. Destructive statements
are denied by default; a DELETE/UPDATE without a WHERE clause is always denied.
Statements on a non-production target can be allowed with a `--allow-destructive`
flag that requires a human confirmation token.
resources.example: `DROP TABLE prod.orders` from an agent is denied and surfaced for confirmation.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: Production Write Confirmation
resources.description: Force human confirmation for any write against a production data target.
resources.summary: Force human confirmation for any write against a production data target.
resources.purpose: Force human confirmation for any write against a production data target.
resources.implementation:
Classify the tool target as production by connection string, project or
catalogue tag. Any write-class tool against a production target is suspended
and surfaced for a human "approve once" token scoped to the single call.
resources.example: An agent asked to run a MERGE on prod.sales is suspended pending approval.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: Secret Scan on Commit
resources.description: Stop credentials from being committed into a pipeline repo.
resources.summary: Stop credentials from being committed into a pipeline repo.
resources.purpose: Stop credentials from being committed into a pipeline repo.
resources.implementation:
Scan staged diffs for high-confidence secret patterns (AWS keys, private key
headers, connection strings with passwords, JWTs). Entropy-based detection runs
as a warning; pattern matches block the commit.
resources.example: A hardcoded `postgresql://user:pass@...` in a notebook is blocked.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: dbt Full-Refresh Guard
resources.description: Require confirmation before a full-refresh of a large incremental model.
resources.summary: Require confirmation before a full-refresh of a large incremental model.
resources.purpose: Require confirmation before a full-refresh of a large incremental model.
resources.implementation:
Inspect dbt commands for `--full-refresh`. If any affected model exceeds a row
threshold (from the manifest's stats) or is tagged `critical`, require an
explicit confirmation token and log the operator identity.
resources.example: `dbt run --full-refresh --select fct_orders` on a 4B-row model is paused for confirmation.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: Freshness Pre-Merge Check
resources.description: Warn when a change would silently widen the freshness SLA of a source.
resources.summary: Warn when a change would silently widen the freshness SLA of a source.
resources.purpose: Warn when a change would silently widen the freshness SLA of a source.
resources.implementation:
Compare the schedule/cron in the diff with the source's declared freshness SLA.
If the new schedule can produce data older than the SLA (e.g. daily when the
SLA is 6h), warn with the computed worst-case lag.
resources.example: Changing a source cron from hourly to daily warns that the 6h freshness SLA will be violated.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: Pre-deployment DQ Check
resources.description: Run the quality suite against a staged run before promoting to production.
resources.summary: Run the quality suite against a staged run before promoting to production.
resources.purpose: Run the quality suite against a staged run before promoting to production.
resources.implementation:
After a pipeline writes to the staging namespace, run the model's dbt/GE tests
against the staged output. Promote only if all critical tests pass; otherwise
leave the previous production data in place and report the failed expectations.
resources.example: A not-null test fails on 412 rows in staging → promotion blocked, production untouched.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: Schema Change Check
resources.description: Block a commit that introduces a breaking schema change without a migration plan.
resources.summary: Block a commit that introduces a breaking schema change without a migration plan.
resources.purpose: Block a commit that introduces a breaking schema change without a migration plan.
resources.implementation:
Runs on staged schema files (*.avsc, *.sql DDL, dbt schema.yml).
Diffs against HEAD, classifies the change, and exits non-zero on a breaking
change unless a MIGRATION.md or a `deprecated_at` annotation is present.
resources.example: A commit narrowing `amount` from decimal(18,2) to decimal(10,2) is blocked with an explanation and a suggested migration.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: Backfill Safety Check
resources.description: Refuse to start a backfill that lacks a rollback path or overlaps the daily run.
resources.summary: Refuse to start a backfill that lacks a rollback path or overlaps the daily run.
resources.purpose: Refuse to start a backfill that lacks a rollback path or overlaps the daily run.
resources.implementation:
Intercepts a backfill trigger. Requires: an explicit date range, a target that
is either a shadow table or snapshotted, and a window that does not overlap the
scheduled production run. Denies otherwise.
resources.example: A bare `airflow dags backfill --start-date 2024-01-01` is denied for missing a range and rollback.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: PII Leak Guard
resources.description: Prevent raw PII from entering model context or being written to an unprotected path.
resources.summary: Prevent raw PII from entering model context or being written to an unprotected path.
resources.purpose: Prevent raw PII from entering model context or being written to an unprotected path.
resources.implementation:
Wrap database/sample tools. Inspect returned rows against the column
classification tags; if a column is classified PII and not masked, redact the
value in the tool response and log the access. Block writes of PII to any path
not tagged as restricted.
resources.example: A `select * from customers` returns an email column; values are redacted before the agent sees them.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: Spark Cost Check
resources.description: Fail a build when a Spark job's shuffle/spill/scan metrics regress past a threshold.
resources.summary: Fail a build when a Spark job's cost metrics regress past a threshold.

limitations: Needs prior runs to build its 5-run baseline, so a cold start has nothing to compare against.

resources.purpose: Fail a build when a Spark job's cost metrics regress past a threshold.
resources.implementation:
After the job's test run, read shuffle/spill/scan metrics from the event log,
compare against the stored baseline (median of last 5), and fail if any metric
grew by more than 25%. Emit the offending stage and metric.
resources.example: Shuffle write grows 3.9x after a join change → build fails with the stage id.
resources.author: de-agent

resources.title: dbt → warehouse → tests → docs
resources.description: Transform raw landed data into a tested, documented star schema with dbt, and gate every change on data-aware CI.

resources.architecture:
raw.orders ─▶ stg_orders ─▶ int_orders_enriched ─┐
raw.customers ─▶ stg_customers ──────────────────┼─▶ fct_orders ─▶ marts
seeds/ ─▶ dim_date ──────────────────────────────┘
            (tests + docs on every node; CI on staging schema)

  models/staging/
  models/intermediate/
  models/marts/
  models/schema.yml     # tests + descriptions
  tests/                # singular tests
  .github/workflows/ci.yml
setup: dbt docs generate && dbt docs serve

implementation.Staging: rename, cast, one row per source row.

implementation.Intermediate: business logic, no direct consumer reads.

implementation.Marts: fct vs dim, grain declared in schema.yml.

implementation: Incremental on fct_orders with a 3-day lookback.
tests: unique + not_null on the fct grain key
failure_scenarios: Late-arriving order missed → lookback window too short
Grain key not unique → a join fanned out upstream

resources.title: API → S3 → Spark → Parquet
resources.description: Land a paginated REST API into S3 raw, transform with PySpark into partitioned Parquet, and make the whole thing idempotent and testable offline.
learning_objectives: Handle pagination, retries and rate limits correctly
Write an idempotent partition overwrite
Test a Spark transform without a cluster
resources.architecture:
REST API ─▶ [extract: paginate + retry] ─▶ S3 raw/ (JSON, immutable)
                                                  │
                                                  ▼
                                 [PySpark transform: type, dedupe, partition]
                                                  │
                                                  ▼
                                 S3 curated/ (Parquet, dt=.., Hive layout)
resources.repo_structure:
api-s3-spark-parquet/
  extract/api_client.py     # pagination, backoff, idempotency key
  transform/orders.py       # typed, deduped, partitioned
  extract/land_raw.py       # writes raw JSON, never overwrites silently
  tests/data/*.json         # tiny fixtures
  tests/test_orders.py
  docker-compose.yml        # minio + spark local
  Makefile
setup: make up  # starts MinIO + a local Spark
make seed  # uploads sample raw JSON
make test  # runs the transform tests offline
implementation: Extract with an explicit cursor and a max-pages guard; log every request.
Land raw JSON untouched, keyed by ingestion date.

implementation.Transform: cast types explicitly, dedupe on the business key, add dt.

implementation: Write Parquet with INSERT OVERWRITE on dt so re-runs are safe.
tests: row count stable across two runs (idempotency)
no nulls in the business key
partition dt matches the logical date, not the wall clock
failure_scenarios: API returns 429 → backoff then resume from the last cursor, not from page 1
A page arrives with a changed field type → quarantine the page, alert
A re-run for the same date duplicates rows → the overwrite is not partition-scoped
production_hardening: Alert on extract lag and on null business keys
Checksum raw files; store the API's cursor for replay

batch ─▶ [contract check] ─┬─ pass ─▶ published/ (SLA-bearing)
                           └─ fail ─▶ quarantine/ (+reason, +source_file)

pipeline-dq-quarantine/
  contract/orders.yml       # rules: not_null, unique, range, enum
  src/validate.py
  src/publish.py
  tests/test_quarantine.py

setup: make test  # validates against the fixtures offline
implementation: Load the contract, compile rules to SQL (DuckDB) or Spark expressions.
Split into pass/fail with a stable `failure_reason`.
Publish the pass set; write the fail set to quarantine with provenance.
tests: every row is either published or quarantined — never lost
the quarantine contains exactly the seeded bad rows
a clean batch produces an empty quarantine
failure_scenarios: Contract too strict → quarantine rate explodes; tier rules and loosen with evidence
Quarantine never reviewed → add a scheduled review and a reprocess path
production_hardening: Alert when quarantine rate > 1% for 2 consecutive runs
A reprocess command that re-runs the quarantined rows after a fix

resources.title: Pipeline failed
resources.description: A task or DAG run has failed and downstream work is blocked — triage, classify and recover.
when_to_use: A task or DAG run failed and downstream work is blocked
An alert fired and someone must decide retry vs fix now
symptoms: A task or DAG run is in a failed state
Downstream tasks are skipped/upstream_failed
An alert has fired
possible_causes: Transient (network, throttling) — retry is enough
Code/resource error — retry will not help
Data error (bad input) — needs a fix upstream or a quarantine
diagnosis: Read the task log and find the first real error, not the last.
Check whether a re-run is safe (idempotency).
commands: -- read the task log via the UI or the log file path in the task instance
fix: Transient → clear and retry the task.
Deterministic → fix the code, redeploy, re-run from the failed task.
Data → fix or quarantine the input, then re-run idempotently.
prevention: Idempotent tasks so a re-run is always safe.
Retries with backoff and a clear failure classification in the alert.
monitoring: task failure rate, DAG run duration, SLA misses
gotchas: Read the first real error in the log, not the last.
Retrying a data error re-runs the same failure; fix or quarantine the input first.
A re-run is only safe if the task is idempotent — check before clearing.
production_notes: Make every task idempotent so a re-run is always safe.
Retry with backoff, and put the failure class in the alert text.
resources.why: The first minute of a pipeline incident decides its length — classify transient, deterministic or data before touching anything, or you re-run the wrong branch all morning.
resources.diagram:
pipeline failed
   |
   |- transient --> clear + retry
   |
   |- code --> fix --> redeploy --> re-run from failed task
   |
   |- data --> fix or quarantine input --> idempotent re-run
tradeoffs: pro: idempotent tasks turn incidents into routine re-runs
con: idempotency costs an upsert/overwrite pattern on every write
resources.impact: Downstream tasks sit skipped/upstream_failed; the SLA miss cascades until the failure is classified and recovered.
resources.escalation: Follow the alert's failure class; page the on-call only for deterministic or data errors on critical paths — transient errors belong to retry policy.
evidence_to_collect: The FIRST real error in the task log (not the last)
The task's idempotency status before any clear-and-retry
Upstream data state for data-class failures
resources.rollback: Roll back the code deploy if the class is deterministic and new; data errors get quarantine-then-retry, not rollback.
follow_up: Make the failed task idempotent if it wasn't
Put the failure class into the alert text

diagnosis: Correlate the first failing signal with the deployment timestamp.
Identify the exact changed artifact and its blast radius.
Confirm the previous version is a valid rollback target.

fix: Roll back the artifact first, then diagnose at leisure.
If data was written, roll back the code and re-run the affected period.

monitoring: deploy markers on dashboards, post-deploy quality gates
gotchas: Roll back before you root-cause; a known-good target is worth more than the diagnosis.
Config changes count: timezone or cluster settings produce invisible regressions.
If bad data was written, rolling back code isn't enough — re-run the affected period.
production_notes: Run tests against a staged build in CI, not production.
Deploy pipelines like services: small diffs, reversible, observable.

bad deployment
   |
   |- first failing signal --> deploy timestamp --> exact changed artifact
   |
   |- previous-good exists --> rollback --> diagnose --> re-run affected period
tradeoffs: pro: rollback restores consumers in minutes
con: rollback discards any good changes shipped in the same window

resources.escalation: Page the on-call and the deploying team; declare an incident when quality gates degrade post-promotion.
evidence_to_collect: The deploy timestamp vs the first failing signal
git log / dbt state:modified+ diff identifying the changed artifact
Confirmation the previous version is a valid rollback target
resources.rollback: Roll back the artifact FIRST, diagnose after; if bad data was written, also re-run the affected period from the rolled-back code.
follow_up: Move tests to a staged build in CI, not production

resources.title: Data contract broken
resources.description: A producer violated its contract and a consumer broke in production — bound the impact before fixing.

symptoms: A consumer's pipeline fails after a producer deploy
A promised column or semantic changed
An SLA (freshness/completeness) is breached
possible_causes: Producer shipped a breaking change without the notice period
A "safe" rename that changed semantics
SLA breach from an unrelated upstream outage
diagnosis: Identify which contract clause broke (schema, semantics, or SLA).
Establish the impact set from lineage before anything else.
Determine if the fix is on the producer (revert) or consumer (adapt).

fix: Schema breach → producer reverts or adds a compatibility shim.
SLA breach → negotiate a temporary relaxation and a root-cause fix.
prevention: Contracts with CI enforcement and a dated deprecation path.
Consumer-driven contract tests in the producer's pipeline.
monitoring: contract-violation events, SLA breach count per asset
gotchas: A 'safe' rename that changed semantics is still a breach.
SLA misses can come from unrelated outages — root-cause before pointing at the producer.
Whatever the fix, the consumer impact set comes first, from lineage.
production_notes: Contracts get CI enforcement and a dated deprecation path.
Run consumer-driven contract tests in the producer's pipeline.
resources.why: A broken contract is a negotiation as much as a bug — bound the blast radius from lineage before deciding who reverts and who adapts.
resources.diagram:
contract broken
   |
   |- schema breach --> producer reverts or adds a compatibility shim
   |
   |- semantic change --> agree semantics --> version the contract
   |
   |- SLA breach --> negotiate temporary relaxation --> root-cause fix
tradeoffs: pro: consumer-driven tests catch breakage before deploy
con: contract overhead slows fast-moving producers
resources.impact: A consumer is down or wrong in production; trust in the contract process itself takes the bigger hit.
resources.escalation: Put the producer and consumer owners on the same call — revert-vs-adapt is a joint decision; escalate to the data platform lead if no agreement within the hour.
evidence_to_collect: The broken clause (schema, semantics, or SLA) and its version history
The lineage-derived impact set for the affected asset
The producer deploy that coincides with the break
resources.rollback: Producer reverts or adds a shim; SLA breaches get a dated temporary relaxation, never an indefinite one.
follow_up: Add the consumer-driven contract test to the producer's pipeline
Record the negotiated semantics as a new contract version

gotchas: Loosening a threshold to silence an alarm is only right with evidence it was a false positive.

Row counts affected, plus sample rows
The distribution shift vs the last good run

resources.title: Duplicate records
resources.description: Row counts are inflated and metrics double-counted after a retry, a fan-out join or a backfill.
when_to_use: Row counts are inflated and metrics double-counted
A unique-key test starts failing after a retry, join change or backfill

Revenue/metrics double-counted
A unique-key test starts failing
possible_causes: A retried task appended instead of overwriting the partition
A join fanned out (non-unique key on the "one" side)
A backfill re-inserted rows that already existed
Exactly-once not achieved in a streaming write
diagnosis: Identify the duplicate key and count duplicates per key.
Determine the earliest date duplicates appeared → correlate with a deploy.
Check whether the write is append vs merge/overwrite.
commands: SELECT k, count(*) c FROM t GROUP BY k HAVING count(*) > 1 ORDER BY c DESC LIMIT 20;
SELECT min(dt), max(dt) FROM (SELECT dt, k, count(*) FROM t GROUP BY dt, k HAVING count(*)>1);
fix: Deduplicate on the business key, keeping the latest by event time.
Rewrite the affected partitions (overwrite), not the whole table.
prevention: Idempotent writes (partition overwrite or MERGE on the key).
A `unique` test on the grain key in CI and in production.
monitoring: duplicate-rate per key, row count vs source count
gotchas: Fix the destination partitions, not the whole table — a full rewrite is both slow and a new risk.
An append instead of overwrite on retry is the classic maker of duplicates.
A non-unique 'one' side in a join fans out silently; test the grain, not the totals.
production_notes: Idempotent writes: partition overwrite or MERGE on the business key.
Run a unique test on the grain key in CI and in production.

resources.diagram:
duplicates
   |
   |- min duplicate date --> correlate with deploy --> fix write mode --> overwrite partitions
   |
   |- fan-out join --> dedupe or fix the grain --> re-run affected range
tradeoffs: pro: MERGE on the key makes retries harmless
con: MERGE needs a solid key; a weak key hides duplicates instead of fixing them
resources.impact: Revenue and usage metrics double-count; finance and product dashboards disagree with each other and with the source.
resources.escalation: Notify metric consumers immediately that published numbers are wrong; bring in the owning team for the write-mode fix.
evidence_to_collect: Duplicate counts per key, and the earliest duplicate date
The deploy or change correlated with that date
The write mode (append vs overwrite/MERGE) of the affected job
resources.rollback: Roll back the write-mode change; then rewrite only the affected partitions, deduplicating by latest event time.
follow_up: Add the unique-grain test in CI and in production

monitoring: max file lateness, count of late arrivals per run

Scheduling the job before the partner's SLA window closes guarantees an incident every day.

Make writes idempotent keyed by business date so a re-run is safe.

con: each widened window re-reads N days of data every run

The job schedule vs the contractual delivery time
Which partitions were reprocessed, and when

resources.title: Missing partition
resources.description: An expected date partition is absent, so a downstream report silently excludes a day.
when_to_use: A date partition is absent and reports quietly exclude a day

A downstream report silently excludes a day

The job wrote to the wrong date due to timezone handling
A partially failed run left an empty or absent partition

Check the job's logical date vs UTC vs local conversion.
Confirm whether the source actually had data.

Backfill the gap partition with the corrected timezone mapping.

Store the logical date explicitly as a partition column, not derived at read time.
monitoring: partition count per day, completeness assertions
gotchas: Confirm the source actually had data before backfilling — otherwise you bake the gap in.
Timezones: job logical date vs UTC vs local — diff all three before re-running.
An empty partition and an absent partition both read as 'no data' downstream.

Store the logical date as a partition column; never derive it at read time.

The job run's logical date, UTC and local timestamps
Source-side proof the data existed (or didn't) for that date

resources.title: Schema drift
resources.description: The upstream schema changed without notice and a cast broke or a column silently nulled.
when_to_use: A column appeared, disappeared or changed type upstream without notice
A pipeline fails on a cast or silently nulls a column
symptoms: A column appears, disappears, or changes type upstream without notice
A pipeline fails on a cast, or silently nulls a column
Catalogue schema and file schema disagree

A new column was added dynamically by the source
Type widened upstream (int → decimal) and broke a cast

Determine whether the failure is hard (job error) or silent (nulls).
commands: -- Glue/Athena: compare catalog columns to the Parquet footer
fix: Additive change → evolve the schema forward (safe) and register it.
Type change → cast explicitly, or reject and quarantine.
Rename/removal → this is breaking; coordinate with consumers.

Alert on any schema delta, even additive ones.
monitoring: schema-hash per source, drift events, quarantine counts
gotchas: Silent nulls are the dangerous case — the job stays green while the column dies.
Renames are removals in disguise; treat them as breaking.
Type widening upstream (int to decimal) breaks the narrow cast downstream.
production_notes: Enforce a schema contract with a compatibility policy in CI.
Alert on any schema delta, even additive ones.
resources.why: An uncontracted schema change is a loaded gun in the pipeline — hard casts break loudly, silent nulls break worse.

schema drift
   |
   |- additive --> evolve contract forward --> register
   |
   |- type change --> explicit cast, or reject + quarantine
   |
   |- rename / removal --> coordinate with consumers --> coordinated cutover

con: strict contracts push work onto producers, who may not have the time

resources.escalation: Contact the producer team immediately with the schema diff; escalate if they cannot revert before the next consumer run.

The failing job's error, or the null-rate delta on affected columns
The contract version the producer was expected to honor

The write jobs feeding the table (stream cadence, micro-batch size)

resources.title: Warehouse query is slow

Review query history weekly for the top cost queries.

Review weekly query history for the top-cost queries.

query slow

con: reclustering rewrites storage and burns credits
